learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected 8.33 dollars and locked it in.
observations.exploration: Equal ten-dollar prices gave thirty shares and both averages ten. Middle five gave forty shares, price average 8.33 and cost per share 7.50. Middle twenty gave twenty-five shares, price average 13.33 and cost per share twelve. Restored ten to confirm equality, then five for reveal.
observations.reveal: Corrected to 7.50, explained ten/twenty/ten shares and three hundred divided by forty. Low-price month buys more shares and gets more weight. Explicit arithmetic-only model with invented prices and no return or purchase claim.
observations.visual: Actual dark 1257 by 936 screenshots inspected. Three share-count bars labeled ten, twenty, ten alongside price labels; average-price and cost-per-share chips distinct and reveal readable.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner said history and analytics are not saved.
observations.blinding: No source, builder notes or other reviews inspected.

prediction.reason: Concrete average choice targets wrong weighting.

interaction.reason: Low, equal and high middle prices isolate share-quantity weighting.
interaction.evidence: Forty, thirty and twenty-five total shares.

payoff.reason: Reveal explains correct denominator through visible purchased quantities.

clarity.reason: Both averages are labeled and arithmetic-only boundary explicit.
clarity.evidence: Invented prices and no return claim.

transfer.reason: General equal-dollar weighting stated without a new application.

accessibility.evidence: Text chips and button states observed; keyboard, screen reader, contrast and reduced motion unaudited.

surprise.reason: Average cost is lower than plain price average.

visualExplanation.reason: More shares in low-price month makes unequal weights visible.
visualExplanation.evidence: Middle bar twice the other two.

practicalValue.reason: Clarifies averaging a unit purchase cost.

depth.reason: One weighting distinction with equal-price boundary.
depth.evidence: Equal dollars versus equal share quantities.

complexity.reason: Simple monetary division and clear bars support weighted-average reasoning.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Choose units purchased as denominator rather than averaging listed prices.
complexity.interfaceBurden: One middle-price slider and three presets.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Share quantity weighting explained with familiar spending.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Dollar prices, unit counts and division.

whyCool: A cheaper month counts more because the same dollars buy more units.
caveat: This demonstrates purchase-cost arithmetic, not return improvement or a recommended investment strategy.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
